chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who drank a sip of wine. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is to be whipped eighty lashes. A little of it or more of it is Prohibited.'
ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed punishment for drinking wine in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the fixed penalty of eighty lashes applies to wine consumption regardless of quantity, emphasizing that the prohibition is absolute even for a mere 'mouthful' (huswa). This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the hadd for khamr is not contingent on reaching a specific volume threshold, distinguishing it from other consumables where quantity might affect liability. The hadith highlights the severity of the prohibition by linking the physical penalty directly to the act of ingestion itself.
